probe: M022 T010 — the inspected page's footprint with and without the overlay, and the tool-element count across a second boot
criterion: SC5 (the ɵsetProfiler list and the feature fingerprint read the same with and without the overlay installed) and SC4's page-visible half (exactly one tool-created element across a second boot)
harness: extension/page-footprint.test.mjs — jsdom under node:test; this file is compared with the measurement on every run, so a stale or hand-written recording fails instead of being quoted

mechanism.arms: Two arms, one page shape. Each arm boots the two ISOLATED-world modules the overlay's own content_scripts declaration shares with it (observer-filter.js, then overlay-geometry.js) and then the MAIN-world recorder (agent-main.js). The withOverlay arm boots overlay.js between them, in the manifest's document_start → document_idle order, so overlay.js is the only variable between the arms.
mechanism.profilerList: The page's `ng` is a stub whose `ɵsetProfiler` records every subscriber it is handed instead of calling it. A second subscriber is a second array entry, so 'the overlay subscribed' is a count and not a claim.
mechanism.featureRecord: The recorder dispatches `angular-ai:state` on the page's own window; the test captures it through a platform listener and compares the `features` object, which is eight `typeof` reads on that same `ng`.
mechanism.pageGlobals: The own property names of `window` added over a baseline taken after the page's `ng` and console exist and before any content script boots.
mechanism.pageNodes: Every element node outside the tool's host subtree, as tag#id.class. The one element the overlay creates is the host, and the host subtree is excluded by construction; the AR-3 count is the separate second-boot reading below.
mechanism.biteProof: Four mutations of overlay.js — a profiler subscription, a deleted `ɵgetSignalGraph`, a written page global, a node appended outside the host subtree — each redden the surface it should, and each test first asserts the same comparison is green without the bite.

doesNotSettle: The realm boundary itself. jsdom has one realm, so the two ISOLATED-world namespace objects (angularAiObserverFilter, angularAiOverlayGeometry) appear as page globals here; in the shipped extension the page's MAIN world cannot read an isolated-world global. Both arms load those two modules, so the differential charges them to neither arm, and the boundary is proven where it exists: the browser check reads the tool-element count on a served page (spikes/probes/overlay-pick.js, toolElements per load and after a reload).

Angular's own dev-mode counters. The stub `ng` carries `ɵsetProfiler` and the seven `typeof` surfaces `featuresOf` reads and nothing else, so 'the dev-mode counters read the same' is a browser reading, not this one; the profiler list and the feature fingerprint are the two halves SC5 names.
Memory, timing and listener-count footprint. The overlay's cost to the page is measured here only as observable state (globals, DOM nodes, profiler subscribers, features).

A live extension re-injection. The second boot here is a second evaluation of overlay.js in the same document, which is the shape a content-script re-run takes; a `chrome.scripting.executeScript` injection over a running extension cannot be driven from jsdom and is the wave-gate browser check's reading.
